title: Pro-etale direct image commutes with uniformly bounded-below coproducts
statement:
Let $h:T\to U$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], meaning that inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact and the diagonal is quasi-compact. Use the small pro-etale sites and universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R_U$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebras on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, set $R_T=h^{-1}R_U$, and use the module sheaves and ordinary uncompleted derived operations [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every small set $I$, integer $N$, and family $K_i\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$ with $H^n(K_i)=0$ for all $n<N$ and $i\in I$, the canonical map induced by the coproduct inclusions is an isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}Rh_*K_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*\left(\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i\right).$$
Here coproducts are the sheafified termwise direct sums of complexes in the indicated derived module categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful].

proof.text: Choose for every K_i a strict >=N complex representative and resolve it by a complex E_i of injectives with the same lower bound. Each E_i is K-injective. The source and target derived module categories have I-indexed coproducts; Q takes a termwise coproduct cocone to a derived coproduct cocone.

source.place: Tag 09A3, objects concentrated in degree zero; Tags 09A1 and 09A2 for the hypercover calculation and Modules on Sites Tag 0935 for sections of sums

proof.text: Apply the module cohomology coproduct theorem to F=h_* in every degree q. For q=0, the canonical natural isomorphism F.rightDerived 0 ≅ F gives underived coproduct preservation. For positive q, the image of every injective E_i^n is zero. The image of their sum is a coproduct of zero objects, hence zero. Evaluation identifies the n-th term of the termwise sum with that sum, so every term of the sum is F-acyclic. The termwise sum remains strictly >=N for the same zero-object argument.

proof.text: Resolve the sum S by a complex J of injectives with the same bound. The resolution map f:S→J is a quasi-isomorphism between bounded-below F-acyclic complexes, so F(f) is a quasi-isomorphism. In the naturality square of the unbounded derived unit, the maps localized from f and F(f) are invertible, and the unit at the K-injective J is invertible. Cancel the right vertical map to conclude the unit at S is invertible.

source.place: Tag 09A3, objects concentrated in degree zero; Tags 09A1 and 09A2 for the hypercover calculation and Modules on Sites Tag 0935 for sections of sums

proof.text: Let v(K):Q(F(K))→RF(Q(K)) be the derived unit transported through the standard quotientCompQhIso. Its naturality is proved explicitly from naturality of those comparison isomorphisms. Every v(E_i) and v(S) is invertible. The termwise-image coproduct is a colimit because F preserves coproducts, and its Q-image is a derived coproduct. Transport that cocone through the natural isomorphism with components v(E_i) and point isomorphism v(S). Naturality identifies the transported coprojections with RF applied to the original coprojections. This proves preservation of the coproduct of Q(E_i), and transport along the chosen representative isomorphisms proves it for K_i.

proof.text: Choose the standard coproduct s of K_i, and choose t to be its image under RF, with the just-proved colimit property. The canonical comparison ht.desc t is the identity by ht.hom_ext. It is an isomorphism, giving all the existential witnesses in the unchanged statement, including for I empty.
